info.title: Paylink Payment Integration API
info.description:
## Overview

The Paylink Payment Integration API enables merchants to seamlessly integrate secure payment processing into their applications. This API follows a simple yet robust flow that handles payment initialization, processing, and completion notifications.

## How It Works

### 1. **Payment Initialization**
Merchants call the `/api/integration/init` endpoint with customer details, order information, and a security signature. This creates a secure checkout session and returns:
- A hosted checkout URL where customers complete their payment
- A unique invoice ID for tracking
- An expiration timestamp for the payment session

### 2. **Customer Payment Flow**
Customers are redirected to the provided checkout URL where they:
- Review their order details
- Select their preferred payment method
- Complete the payment securely on Paylink's hosted page

### 3. **Real-time Notifications (Webhooks)**
As the payment progresses through different states, Paylink automatically sends POST requests to your configured webhook URL for enabled event types:
- `invoice.paid` / `invoice.not_paid` (enabled by default)
- `invoice.voided` / `invoice.refunded` / `invoice.authorization_reversed` (opt-in)

Each webhook includes an `event` field, transaction details (including the gateway `auth_code` when available), and HMAC signatures for security verification. Configure which events trigger webhooks under **Settings → Payment Integrations → Webhook Events**.

### 4. **Customer Return (Website or Mobile App)**
After payment completion — on both **success and failure** — the customer is returned to the destination determined by your integration's **Type**:
- **Website** integrations return the customer to your configured **Redirect URL** (e.g. `https://mywebsite.com/return`).
- **Mobile App** integrations return the customer to your app through the configured **Mobile App Return Scheme**, a custom-scheme deep link (e.g. `payindemo://payment-return`).

In both cases the same transaction details are delivered as query parameters:
- Transaction results as URL parameters
- Status information (completed/failed/cancelled)
- Security signature for verification

## Key Features

- **🔒 Security First**: All requests and callbacks use HMAC-SHA256 signatures for verification
- **⚡ Real-time Updates**: Instant webhook notifications for all transaction events
- **🌍 Multi-currency**: Support for EGP, EUR, and USD
- **📱 Hosted Checkout**: No PCI compliance burden - customers pay on Paylink's secure pages
- **🔄 Automatic Retries**: Failed webhook deliveries are retried up to 5 times
- **⚙️ Admin Configuration**: Integration type, webhook URL, redirect URL, and mobile app return scheme are configured once in your dashboard

## Configuration Requirements

Before using this API, ensure you have configured the following in your Paylink dashboard:
- **Type**: `Website` or `Mobile App` — determines where customers are returned after payment
- **Webhook URL**: Where you'll receive transaction status updates
- **Redirect URL**: Where website customers return after payment completion
- **Mobile App Return Scheme**: (Mobile App integrations only) the custom-scheme deep link your app is returned to after payment
- **Hash Token**: Used for generating and verifying HMAC signatures
- **Webhook Events**: Choose which events trigger notifications (defaults: `invoice.paid`, `invoice.not_paid`)

## Authentication

This API uses token-based authentication combined with HMAC signatures:
- **Authentication Token**: Included in API requests for identification
- **Hash Token**: Used for signature generation (keep this secret)
- **Signatures**: Required for all requests and verified on all callbacks

---

## Getting Started

Follow these steps to set up your payment integration:

### Step 1: Get Your API Credentials
1. Log in to your Paylink dashboard
2. Navigate to **Settings → Payment Integrations**
3. Click **Add Integration** to create a new integration
4. Fill in the integration details:
   - **Name**: A friendly name for this integration (e.g., "My Website Checkout")
   - **Origin**: The domain of your website (e.g., `https://mywebsite.com`)
   - **Type**: `Website` or `Mobile App`. Choose **Mobile App** only when customers pay inside a native app; choose **Website** for browser-based checkouts. Existing integrations created before this option default to **Website**.
   - **Webhook URL**: The endpoint on your server that will receive payment notifications
   - **Redirect URL**: Where website customers are sent after completing payment
   - **Mobile App Return Scheme**: (Mobile App integrations only) the custom-scheme deep link your app is returned to, e.g. `payindemo://payment-return`
5. After saving, you'll receive:
   - **Authentication Token**: Used in API requests to identify your integration
   - **Hash Token**: Used to generate HMAC signatures (keep this secret!)

### Step 2: Configure Your Server
- Set up your **Webhook endpoint** to receive POST requests with transaction updates
- Set up your **Redirect page** to handle customers returning from the checkout
- Store your **Hash Token** securely (environment variable recommended)

### Step 3: Make Your First Request
Use the `/api/integration/init` endpoint below to create a checkout session, then redirect the customer to the returned `checkout_url`.

---

## Testing Cards

In the **sandbox/test environment**, payment outcomes are driven by the **transaction amount** and by the card data you enter - not by special "decline card numbers". Use a valid test card from the table below and set the amount to a trigger value to simulate an approval or a specific decline.

> **Important:** Test cards from other providers (for example `4000 0000 0000 0127` or `4000 0000 0000 0069`) do **not** work here. The sandbox authorizes any well-formed card number, so they return a successful/PAID result. Use the cards and amounts on this page instead.

### Test Cards

| Card Type | Card Number | Expiry | CVV |
|-----------|-------------|--------|-----|
| Visa | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | Any future date | Any 3 digits |
| Mastercard | 5555 5555 5555 4444 | Any future date | Any 3 digits |
| Mastercard (2-series) | 2222 4200 0000 1113 | Any future date | Any 3 digits |

### Simulating Declines

Use any valid test card above and set the **transaction amount** to one of these values to force a specific decline:

| Amount | Result |
|--------|--------|
| 4051.00 | Insufficient funds |
| 4054.00 | Expired card |
| 4005.00 | Do not honor (general decline) |
| 4043.00 | Stolen card |
| 4041.00 | Lost card |
| 7001.00 | Rejected - invalid card |

You can also force a failure with invalid card data:

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Card `4111 1111 1111 1112` (invalid checksum) | Declined |
| Past expiry year (e.g. `1998`) | Declined |
| Amount `-1` or `100000000000` | Invalid request |

A declined payment returns `success=0` and leaves the invoice unpaid - no booking is confirmed.

> **Note:** These triggers work only in the sandbox/test environment, never in production. In production, use real card details.

---

*Ready to get started? Begin with the `/api/integration/init` endpoint below.*## Recurring subscriptions

To charge a customer automatically on a schedule (subscriptions / card-on-file), use the **Recurring Subscriptions** endpoints. The customer authenticates once (3DS) on the first payment; PayLink then charges automatically each cycle and notifies you with signed `subscription.*` webhooks. See the dedicated **Recurring Subscriptions Integration Guide** (`RECURRING_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`, in this docs folder) for a complete step-by-step walkthrough.

tags.description:
Subscription mandate lifecycle endpoints. Create a mandate with the customer's first payment (card vaulted, 3DS-authenticated), then query status or manage the lifecycle (cancel/pause/resume). All endpoints use the same public_token + HMAC-SHA256 signature authentication as the v2 init endpoint. The recurring payments feature must be enabled for your account.

**Webhooks.** Subscription events (`subscription.activated`, `subscription.charged`, `subscription.payment_failed`, `subscription.suspended`, `subscription.cancelled`, `subscription.completed`) are POSTed to your webhook URL. The JSON payload includes `event`, `success`, `invoice_id`, `invoice_status`, `message`, `mandate_id`, `external_reference`, `subscription_status`, an optional `auth_code` (the gateway approval code, present only when available) and `signature`. Correlate a charge to its subscription using `mandate_id` or `external_reference` — not `invoice_id` (each billing cycle bills a new invoice). Verify the signature as Base64(HMAC-SHA256) over the concatenated payload values except `event`, `auth_code` and `signature`, in order: `success, invoice_id, invoice_status, message, mandate_id, external_reference, subscription_status`.

**Full step-by-step guide:** see `RECURRING_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` in this documentation folder.

Optional. A JSON-encoded array of `{label, value}` objects shown on the checkout page, each rendered on its own line (e.g. Guest, Reservation, Room, Check-In, Check-Out). When omitted, the checkout falls back to displaying the single `order_title`. Max 2000 characters.

Payment mode. `capture` (default) charges the customer immediately upon checkout. `authorize` places a hold on the funds without charging — you can then settle (capture) or reverse the authorization using the payment operation endpoints.

**Important:** This field is NOT included in the signature calculation, so it can be added without changing how the signature is generated. Requires the authorize-mode capability to be enabled for your company when using `authorize`.

signature.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signature for request verification. This signature ensures the request authenticity and prevents tampering.

**How to generate the signature:**
1. Concatenate all field values (except 'token' and 'signature') in the exact order they appear in the request
2. Create HMAC-SHA256 hash using your secret hash token (from account settings)
3. Encode the result in base64

**Code Examples:**

**PHP:**
```php
// Step 1: Prepare data (exclude token and signature)
$data = [
    $first_name,
    $last_name, 
    $email,
    $order_title,
    $order_amount,
    $address,     // include even if empty
    $city,        // include even if empty  
    $country,     // include even if empty
    $currency
];

// Step 2: Generate signature
$concatenated = implode('', $data);
$signature = base64_encode(hash_hmac('sha256', $concatenated, $hashKey, true));
```

**Node.js:**
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');

// Step 1: Prepare data array
const data = [
    first_name,
    last_name,
    email, 
    order_title,
    order_amount,
    address || '',   // handle optional fields
    city || '',
    country || '',
    currency
];

// Step 2: Generate signature
const concatenated = data.join('');
const signature = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', hashKey)
    .update(concatenated)
    .digest('base64');
```

**Python:**
```python
import hmac
import hashlib
import base64

# Step 1: Prepare data
data = [
    first_name,
    last_name,
    email,
    order_title, 
    order_amount,
    address or '',   # handle optional fields
    city or '',
    country or '',
    currency
]

# Step 2: Generate signature
concatenated = ''.join(data)
signature = base64.b64encode(
    hmac.new(
        hash_key.encode('utf-8'),
        concatenated.encode('utf-8'),
        hashlib.sha256
    ).digest()
).decode('utf-8')
```

**Important Notes:**
- Use the hash token from your Paylink account settings (not the public token)
- Include optional fields in concatenation even if they're empty strings
- Field order matters - follow the exact sequence shown above
- If you send the optional `state` field, include it in the concatenation immediately after `country` (before `currency`); the code snippets above omit it for brevity
- The signature must be recalculated for every request

Called whenever a transaction status changes for an event your integration is subscribed to. The webhook URL is configured per-integration in the Paylink dashboard, and event types are managed under **Settings → Payment Integrations → Webhook Events** (or **Settings → Webhook Notifications**). By default only `invoice.paid` and `invoice.not_paid` are enabled.

**Available event types (produced by the hosted checkout):**
- `invoice.paid` – Invoice was successfully paid
- `invoice.not_paid` – Payment attempt failed

Every other event (`invoice.voided`, `invoice.refunded`, `invoice.authorization_reversed`, `vcc.payment_success`/`vcc.payment_failed`, `card_token.charge_succeeded`/`card_token.charge_failed`, and the `subscription.*` events) is delivered to this same webhook URL and is documented as a **Callback** on the operation that produces it.

**Server-to-server charges.** VCC (`/api/v2/integration/vcc/charge`) and Card Tokenization (`/api/v2/integration/tokens/charge`) charges are delivered over this same signed integration webhook, verified with the identical signature scheme (`success + invoice_id + invoice_status + message`).

**Paylink expects a 200 OK response; if it does not receive 200, the delivery will be retried up to 3 times with 100ms intervals.**

success.description: Whether the operation was successful (1 for paid/voided/refunded/reversed, 0 for not_paid)

invoice_id.description: The unique identifier of the invoice/transaction

invoice_status.description: Current paid status of the invoice

message.description: Human-readable message or context about the status

auth_code.description: The payment gateway's authorization (approval) code for the transaction. Present only when a successful payment attempt supplied one; omitted otherwise. Excluded from the HMAC signature calculation (like `event`), so it can be consumed without changing signature verification.

signature.description: HMAC signature for webhook verification using the same hash key as the integration. Calculated using SHA256 over the concatenation of: success + invoice_id + invoice_status + message. **Note:** The `event` and `auth_code` fields are excluded from the signature calculation for backward compatibility. Success is sent as integer (1 or 0) in the webhook payload for cross-language compatibility.

**Important:** This field is NOT included in the signature calculation, so it can be added without changing how the signature is generated. Requires the authorize-mode capability to be enabled for your company when using `authorize`.

installments_enabled.description:
Optional. Set to `true` to charge this order as a fixed installment plan (Pay in N) instead of a single payment. The checkout then shows the fixed schedule and an authorisation consent the customer must accept before paying; the first installment is charged at checkout and the remaining installments are scheduled automatically to the saved card. Requires the Installments (Pay in N) capability to be enabled for your company.

**Important:** This field is NOT included in the signature calculation, so it can be added without changing how the signature is generated.

installments.description:
The number of installments for the plan. Required when `installments_enabled` is `true`, and must match one of the installment counts your company offers (the cadence — e.g. monthly — is taken from your company's configured plan for that count). Rejected with a 422 validation error if the count is not offered, the account does not have the Installments capability enabled, or the order amount is below your configured installment minimum.

**Important:** This field is NOT included in the signature calculation.

redirection_url.description: Optional. A per-request URL the customer is redirected to after payment. It MUST use HTTPS and be on the same domain as your integration's Origin (or your configured Redirect URL host). **INCLUDED in the signature on v2.** When omitted, your configured Redirect URL is used. Not supported for Mobile App integrations.

webhook_url.description: Optional. A per-request webhook URL that overrides your configured Webhook URL for this invoice only. It MUST use HTTPS and be on the same domain as your integration's Origin (or your configured Webhook URL host) — other domains are rejected. **INCLUDED in the signature on v2.** When omitted, your configured Webhook URL is used.

signature.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signature that authenticates the request and protects it from tampering. This is the **v2 init** rule — it differs from v1, which does **not** sign `order_details`, `redirection_url`, or `webhook_url`.

**The four rules**

1. **Signed fields** — every field you send **except** `token`, `signature`, `payment_mode`, `installments_enabled`, and `installments`. An optional field you do not send is skipped (it contributes nothing).
2. **Order & separator** — concatenate the values in this fixed order, with **no separator**. This is the server's canonical order, not the order of the keys in your JSON body:

   `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `order_title`, `order_amount`, `address`, `city`, `country`, `state`, `currency`, `redirection_url`, `webhook_url`, `order_details`
3. **Digest** — `HMAC-SHA256(concatenated, hash_token)` over the **raw bytes**, then **Base64** (standard Base64 of the raw digest — not hex, not base64url).
4. **Key** — your secret **hash token** from the integration settings, never the public `token` (which only identifies the integration and is sent unsigned in the body).

**Code Examples:**

**PHP:**
```php
// Signed values, in the fixed order. Use '' for any optional field you don't send.
$data = [
    $first_name,
    $last_name,
    $email,
    $order_title,
    $order_amount,
    $address,          // optional
    $city,             // optional
    $country,          // optional
    $state,            // optional
    $currency,
    $redirection_url,  // optional (v2)
    $webhook_url,      // optional (v2)
    $order_details,    // optional (v2)
];

$signature = base64_encode(hash_hmac('sha256', implode('', $data), $hashToken, true));
```

**Node.js:**
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');

const data = [
    first_name,
    last_name,
    email,
    order_title,
    order_amount,
    address || '',
    city || '',
    country || '',
    state || '',
    currency,
    redirection_url || '',
    webhook_url || '',
    order_details || ''
];

const signature = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', hashToken)
    .update(data.join(''))
    .digest('base64');
```

**Python:**
```python
import hmac, hashlib, base64

data = [
    first_name,
    last_name,
    email,
    order_title,
    str(order_amount),
    address or '',
    city or '',
    country or '',
    state or '',
    currency,
    redirection_url or '',
    webhook_url or '',
    order_details or ''
]

digest = hmac.new(hash_token.encode('utf-8'), ''.join(data).encode('utf-8'), hashlib.sha256).digest()
signature = base64.b64encode(digest).decode('utf-8')
```

**Notes:**
- Use the **hash token** (secret), not the public `token`.
- No separator between values, and sign each value exactly as you send it (e.g. `order_amount` "250" must match the body).
- A field you omit and the same field sent as an empty string produce the same signature, so `... || ''` is always safe.
- `state` is signed (right after `country`). A common cause of "Invalid signature" is signing a US/CA billing state that an older sample leaves out — include it here.
- The digest is Base64 of the **raw** HMAC bytes, not a hex string.
- Recalculate the signature for every request.

post.description:
**Base URL:** `https://pay.getpayin.com`

Charges a Virtual Credit Card (VCC) **server-to-server** using your integration's HMAC signature — no hosted checkout page and no customer redirect. It is the same charge as the dashboard VCC endpoint, only authenticated by the integration `token` + `signature` (identical scheme to `/api/v2/integration/init`), so the request is HMAC-secured.

**Requirements:** Payment Integrations must be enabled for your company, the integration must be active, the **VCC module** must be enabled, and you must hold an active **VCC subscription**. Because raw card data is sent directly to this endpoint, call it **only from your PCI-compliant backend** — never from a browser or mobile client.

**Webhooks:** a successful charge fires the `vcc.payment_success` webhook event and a declined one fires `vcc.payment_failed` — delivered exactly like the dashboard VCC charge.

currency_id.description: PayLink currency id to charge in (the same id used by the VCC and Invoice APIs)

price.description: Amount to charge in major units; must be greater than 0

product.description: Product / order description shown on the invoice

reference_number.description: Your own reference for this charge [OPTIONAL]

country.description: Billing country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. EG, US, CA)

us_state.description: 2-letter US state code. Required and signed only when country = US.

canada_state.description: 2-letter Canadian province code. Required and signed only when country = CA.

postal_code.description: Postal / ZIP code. Required and signed only when country = US or CA.

signature.description:

HMAC-SHA256 signature authenticating the request — identical scheme to `/api/v2/integration/init`, using the **hash token** from your integration settings.

**How to generate:**
1. Concatenate the signed field values (everything except `token` and `signature`) in the exact order below, with no separator. Include the optional fields you send; for any field you omit, concatenate an empty string.
2. HMAC-SHA256 the concatenated string with your secret hash token.
3. Base64-encode the digest.

**Field order:** `invoice_id`.

**PHP:**
```php
$data = [
    $invoice_id,
];
$signature = base64_encode(
    hash_hmac('sha256', implode('', $data), $hashToken, true)
);
```

**Node.js:**
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');
const data = [
    invoice_id
];
const signature = crypto.createHmac('sha256', hashToken)
    .update(data.join(''))
    .digest('base64');
```

**Python:**
```python
import hmac, hashlib, base64
data = [
    str(invoice_id)
]
digest = hmac.new(hash_token.encode(), ''.join(data).encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
signature = base64.b64encode(digest).decode()
```

**Notes:**
- Use the **hash token** (secret), not the public token.
- Numeric values are concatenated exactly as sent — make sure the string form matches your submitted value.
- Recalculate the signature for every request.

post.description:
Creates a subscription mandate and the first setup invoice, returning a signed `checkout_url`. The first charge is customer-present (3DS-authenticated, card vaulted); subsequent charges run unattended on the configured cadence.

**Availability:** Recurring payments must be enabled for your account.

**Idempotency:** The dedup key is `external_reference` when provided; otherwise the `Idempotency-Key` request header is used. Deduplication is scoped to `(company, integration, key)`. A replay with the **same terms** returns the same `mandate_id` and a fresh `checkout_url`. A replay with **different terms** returns `409 Conflict`; the compared terms are `order_amount`, `currency`, `cadence_interval`, `cadence_count`, `total_cycles`, and `end_date`. Reusing a reference whose subscription is `cancelled`, `failed`, or `completed` creates a new subscription (the old mandate is preserved).

**Base URL:** `https://pay.getpayin.com`

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional dedup key used when `external_reference` is not in the request body. If the same key is replayed the original mandate and checkout_url are returned unchanged.

order_title.description: Subscription plan title shown to the subscriber at checkout.

order_amount.description: Amount charged per cycle (must be greater than 0).

currency.description: ISO currency code (e.g. EGP, USD, EUR). Must be a currency supported by your company.

cadence_interval.description: The interval unit for the billing cadence.

cadence_count.description: Number of interval units between charges. E.g. `cadence_count=1` with `cadence_interval=month` = every month; `cadence_count=3` = every quarter.

total_cycles.description: Total number of billing cycles including the setup charge. When null or omitted the subscription continues until cancelled.

end_date.description: Optional hard end date for the subscription (must be a future date). No charge will occur after this date.

consent_text.description: The exact subscription terms text that the cardholder sees and accepts at checkout. Required for regulatory/mandate compliance. Max 2000 characters.
consent_text.example: By subscribing you authorise monthly charges of EGP 99.99 until cancelled.

external_reference.description: Your own subscription identifier. Used as the idempotency key — repeated requests with the same value return the original mandate. When omitted the `Idempotency-Key` header is used instead.

redirection_url.description: Optional HTTPS redirect URL for the customer after the first checkout. Must be on your integration's registered domain. **Included in the signature when provided.**

webhook_url.description: Optional per-request webhook URL override. Must be HTTPS on your integration's registered domain. **Included in the signature when provided.**

signature.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signature for request verification.

**How to generate:**
1. Take all validated request fields in rule-definition order, EXCLUDING `token`, `signature`, and `payment_mode`
2. Concatenate with **no delimiter** in this exact order:
   `first_name + last_name + email + order_title + order_amount + currency + cadence_interval + cadence_count + [total_cycles if provided] + [end_date if provided] + consent_text + [external_reference if provided] + [redirection_url if provided] + [webhook_url if provided]`
3. Nullable fields are included ONLY when present in the request (absent fields are skipped)
4. HMAC-SHA256 over the concatenated string using your hash_token
5. Base64-encode the raw HMAC bytes

**PHP:**
```php
// Build ordered field array, skip null/absent fields
$fields = array_values(array_filter(
    [$first_name, $last_name, $email, $order_title, $order_amount,
     $currency, $cadence_interval, $cadence_count,
     $total_cycles ?? null, $end_date ?? null, $consent_text,
     $external_reference ?? null, $redirection_url ?? null, $webhook_url ?? null],
    fn($v) => $v !== null
));
$signature = base64_encode(hash_hmac('sha256', implode('', $fields), $hashToken, true));
```

**Node.js:**
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');
const fields = [
    first_name, last_name, email, order_title, order_amount,
    currency, cadence_interval, cadence_count,
    ...(total_cycles != null ? [total_cycles] : []),
    ...(end_date != null ? [end_date] : []),
    consent_text,
    ...(external_reference != null ? [external_reference] : []),
    ...(redirection_url != null ? [redirection_url] : []),
    ...(webhook_url != null ? [webhook_url] : []),
];
const signature = crypto.createHmac('sha256', hashToken)
    .update(fields.join('')).digest('base64');
```

**Python:**
```python
import hmac, hashlib, base64
fields = [f for f in [
    first_name, last_name, email, order_title, str(order_amount),
    currency, cadence_interval, str(cadence_count),
    str(total_cycles) if total_cycles is not None else None,
    end_date if end_date is not None else None,
    consent_text,
    external_reference if external_reference is not None else None,
    redirection_url if redirection_url is not None else None,
    webhook_url if webhook_url is not None else None,
] if f is not None]
signature = base64.b64encode(
    hmac.new(hash_token.encode(), ''.join(fields).encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
).decode()
```

post.description:
Charges an installment ahead of schedule on an active installment (Pay in N) plan. The customer can pay **the next installment** or **the entire remaining balance** early.

Returns a signed hosted-checkout URL (valid for 60 minutes) that carries the chosen intent — open it for the customer to complete the on-session payment. After the payment succeeds the plan advances automatically: `next` records the paid cycle and re-anchors the following scheduled charge to the cadence; `remaining` settles every outstanding cycle and completes the plan. The request is refused (422) when the plan is not active, or when the target cycle is already being charged by the scheduler, so an early payment can never double-charge a cycle.

**Signature:** HMAC-SHA256 of the mandate UID only (see Get Mandate Status for code examples).

- `next` — the next scheduled installment only. The plan advances one cycle and the following charge is re-anchored to the cadence.
- `remaining` — the entire outstanding balance across all remaining installments, settling the plan in a single payment.

This field is NOT part of the signature calculation.
